Daylight saving time began at different times depending on the jurisdiction. In Canada, the world’s first daylight saving time period started on July 1, 1908, in Port Arthur, Ontario [d3]. In Germany, daylight saving time was first practically used in 1916 during World War I [d9]. The United States first enacted daylight saving time on March 19, 1918, as a wartime measure [d7], and the Standard Time Act signed by President Woodrow Wilson in 1918 officially recognized it that year [d8][d5].
